text.final_text: "Blanc cassé" … Broken white.

The comma after "Blanc cassé," is also dropped at the cut. In her text only "Blanc cassé" is in quotes because the clerk says it. 'Broken white.' is narration, so the quote marks around it on screen are display styling only. Her Russian has 'Blanc cassé' in Latin letters too, followed by 'Сломанный белый.'

text.final_text: The main and only thing required of you is to create and fiercely protect my silence.

text.note: Exact match to the English Text of #053, paragraph 2. In the story Ule says this to Kira as his condition. The wrapping quote marks are display styling only.

text.scenario_text: "He does not touch her. He simply stands close enough that she feels the heat of his body through the fabric."
text.final_text: He does not touch her. He simply stands close enough that she feels the heat of his body through the fabric.
text.source_text: Ule is silent behind her. His breathing is the only sound in the hall. Like a commit hanging in limbo, waiting for merge. He does not touch her. He simply stands close enough that she feels the heat of his body through the fabric. Agentic. Quiet.
text.note: Exact match to the English Text of #097, paragraph 3. Checked as a programmatic exact-substring match.

text.scenario_text: "I'm a lesbian. Please consider this for possible group activities."
text.final_text: I'm a lesbian. Please consider this for possible group activities.

text.note: Exact match to the English Text of #053, paragraph 3, where Kira answers Mr. Glensdagen. The apostrophe is straight in both the source and the extract.

text.scenario_text: «Поцелуя не жду. Губами / Расцелую я лед на стеклах.» — draft: "I'm not waiting for a kiss. My lips / will cover the ice on the panes with kisses."
text.final_text: I'm not waiting for a kiss. My lips / will cover the ice on the panes with kisses.
text.source_text: Поцелуя не жду. Губами / Расцелую я лед на стеклах.
text.note: The extract line gives no poem number. I found it as the opening two lines of LITPROM #044 'Вчерашний день' in atuona-complete-with-dates.json. The Russian matches exactly, including 'лед' spelled without ё. The source runs the lines together with spaces, but the capital 'Расцелую' marks the line start, which matches the '/' break. #044 is in Russian only. Its 'English Analysis' field is commentary, not a translation. So the English here is a DRAFT, not her words, and Elena must approve it before it goes on screen. Please add the citation (#044) to this line in the scenario.
Shot 5 'The leaf.' has an empty lines array in film9_onscreen_text_extract_2026-10-08.json. There is no on-screen text, voice or speech to check. This record exists only to show the shot was checked.

text.scenario_text: «Море волнуется раз. / Море волнуется два.» — draft: "The sea is stormy — one. / The sea is stormy — two."
text.final_text: The sea is stormy — one. / The sea is stormy — two.
text.source_text: Море волнуется раз. / Море волнуется два.
text.note: The extract line gives no poem number. I found it in LITPROM #004 'Vesenneye'. The Russian matches exactly. The couplet appears twice in #004: it opens the poem, followed by 'Наживка с крючка сорвалась.', and comes back later, followed by 'Доченька родилась.' Next to the following line in this shot, it is the opening stanza. It quotes a children's game, and her poem stops at 'два', never 'три', which fits the shot title. #004 is in Russian only, so the English is a DRAFT. Elena must approve it. The em dashes are draft punctuation and are not in her text. Please add the citation (#004).

text.scenario_text: «Наживка с крючка сорвалась. / Я шлепнулась и уплыла.» — draft: "The bait broke off the hook. / I plopped in and swam away."
text.final_text: The bait broke off the hook. / I plopped in and swam away.
text.source_text: Наживка с крючка сорвалась. / Я шлепнулась и уплыла.
text.note: Lines 3-4 of LITPROM #004 'Vesenneye'. They come directly after the opening 'Море волнуется раз. Море волнуется два.' The Russian matches exactly, with 'шлепнулась' spelled without ё. #004 is in Russian only, so the English is a DRAFT. Elena must approve it. On wording: 'сорвалась' means tore or slipped off the hook, so 'broke off' is a translator's choice. Please add the citation (#004).

text.scenario_text: «Я тебя крылатая, дождусь, / перьями подушку набиваю. / Зря ты снова сбросил чешую / там, где я тихонечко взлетаю.» — draft: "I'll wait for you — winged, / stuffing the pillow with feathers. / For nothing you've shed your scales again / right where I'm ever so quietly taking wing."
text.final_text: I'll wait for you — winged, / stuffing the pillow with feathers. / For nothing you've shed your scales again / right where I'm ever so quietly taking wing.
text.source_text: Я тебя крылатая, дождусь, / перьями подушку набиваю. / Зря ты снова сбросил чешую / там, где я тихонечко взлетаю.
text.note: The extract line gives no poem number. This is the closing quatrain of LITPROM #036 'Азимут'. The Russian matches exactly. The source runs the lines together, and this poem starts its lines in lower case, so I inferred the '/' breaks from the meter. They follow the same alternating 9/10-syllable lines as the poem's opening, 'Зря ты поломал мои крючки. / Рыбы не кончают суицидом.' #036 is in Russian only, so the English is a DRAFT. Elena must approve it. On wording: 'Зря' is closer to 'In vain' than 'For nothing'. 'Я тебя крылатая, дождусь' is literally 'Winged, I will wait for you'. Please add the citation (#036).

text.final_text: Morning in Atuona doesn't begin with light. / It begins with scent.

Morning in Atuona doesn't begin with light.
It begins with scent.

text.final_text: Kira woke to heat. / Sheets stuck to skin like a second dress. / Through the shutters — Atuona morning, thick as honey. / The air tastes of frangipani and rust.

Kira woke to heat.
Sheets stuck to skin like a second dress.
Through the shutters — Atuona morning, thick as honey.
The air tastes of frangipani and rust.

text.poem: #019 «Апокалипсис» (LITPROM, published 15-11-2020) — NOT cited in the extract
text.scenario_text: «Что ж так рвешься в мой плен суровый? / Ну же, с плеч приспусти бретели... / Ради Бога, не будь хладнокровна, / Убивая меня в постели!» — draft: "Why do you strain so toward my harsh captivity? / Come on — slip the straps down off your shoulders... / For God's sake, don't be cold-blooded / killing me in bed!"
text.final_text: Why do you strain so toward my harsh captivity? / Come on — slip the straps down off your shoulders... / For God's sake, don't be cold-blooded / killing me in bed!
text.source_text: Что ж так рвешься в мой плен суровый? / Ну же, с плеч приспусти бретели... / Ради Бога, не будь хладнокровна, / Убивая меня в постели!
text.note: The Russian matches #019 «Апокалипсис» word for word (checked as an exact substring; the published text has no line breaks, so the ' / ' breaks are only layout). The extract does not name the poem, so the citation #019 needs to be added. The poem is Russian only, so the English is a draft Elena has to approve. In the poem these lines are spoken to Тоска (Longing/Melancholy as a person, the feminine 'хладнокровна'), not to a woman. The film uses them as a lover's voice, which is a change of context Elena should approve. Translation point: 'рвешься в' literally means 'rush/strain INTO' my harsh captivity, not 'toward'.

It is a sound cue written as a stage direction, so no words appear on screen; 'the valley church bell strikes three times' is direction wording, not her text. qa.name: k13
qa.why: Kira and Ule match the originals and cast refs, and the framing is the same. But the pass adds things she did not approve: rain-wet skin across her face, chest and leg, a drip falling from her chin, and water dripping off the lantern. The wet sheen makes the skin glossier, not less painted.

qa.name: k14
qa.why: The pass added big glossy cartoon teardrops under both of Kira's eyes and reddened her eyes, so her composed, approved expression is now crying. The drops are a classic AI artifact. Ule, the necklace, the lanterns and the lightning are unchanged.

qa.name: k16m
qa.why: Almost no change: same hands, clasp, emerald necklace, wet back and room. The only difference is slightly lifted exposure and shadows. The original already looks like a film still, so there is nothing to gain. Swapping is harmless but pointless.

qa.name: k17a
qa.why: Kira's face and pose are the same, but the pass added sparkly water drops all over the black dress and a tan sand or stain smear down its front and hem. These are new defects on a clean approved costume. The beach, palms and cliffs are unchanged.

qa.name: k18
qa.why: The composition and carving are the same, but the light changed colour. The warm amber light shaft and golden curtains became a cool teal-cyan film grade with lifted blacks, and the hand turned paler with bigger, separate water beads. A slight film-stock feel does not justify changing the approved light colour.

qa.name: k19
qa.why: The cold blue moonlight on the forearm became neutral or warm daylight, and the dark blue vein, likely a story element, is fainter and softer. The pass also adds a few small red spots. The original macro already reads as real skin.

qa.name: k20
qa.why: The pass added streaming glossy tears down Kira's cheeks, which changes her approved stoic expression. The exposure is also lifted a lot, so the dark chiaroscuro and the mood of the room are gone and her skin looks paler and smoother. The paddles went from textured to flat blank white.

qa.name: k20b
qa.why: This pass gives the biggest realism gain in the set: the original's heavy HDR crunch on his face, arm and shirt is gone, and Ule still matches his locked ref. But the warm golden sun-and-leaf light became cool white-teal, and tear-like drops now run under his eye. Elena should choose, or re-run the pass with the warm grade locked and no drops on the face.

qa.name: k21
qa.why: The content is identical: same hand, scratched book, cobwebs and broken boards, with nothing added. The only change is that the exposure is roughly doubled and the blacks lifted. That gives slightly more film-like detail but weakens the dark crawlspace mood she approved. It is fine to swap if she likes the brighter look or if it is graded back down.

qa.name: k01a
qa.why: Framing, poses and the spray from the lamp are the same, so this pass only changed the colour grade. The warm amber light on the wall and floor turned cool grey-teal (mean blue went from 53 to 70). The original already had real film grain, so the lighting she approved changed with almost no gain in realism.

qa.name: k01b
qa.why: Ule's stubble, lips and necklace match, and the bun and tweed are the same. It looks more like film, with less glassy HDR hair. But the pass removed the blue backlight flare behind her ear and added water drops to her neck, hair, collar and jacket. The wet look does fit the spray in k01a, so Elena should decide.

qa.name: k02
qa.why: The pass added tears: two tracks running from her closed eye down her cheek, plus drops. That changes the emotion of the performance she approved. Her profile, brow scar, window and reflection are the same, and the skin is warmer and less glossy, so a re-run with no tears would probably pass.

qa.name: k05
qa.why: A near-black storm at night became a bright teal dusk sky (mean brightness 42 to 91). The leaf lost its red-against-gold contrast and is now an even copper. The pass also added an orange light leak along the top edge and dust specks. The leaf's shape and the city lights are the same.

qa.name: k06
qa.why: Tears were added under both eyes, which changes the expression. The face still matches Kira's reference (grey-green eyes, wet curls), and the skin has better grain and warmth, but the added tears rule it out. Re-run without tears.

qa.name: k07b
qa.why: The moonlit night turned into a pale blue daytime sky: the moon now reads as a sun and the stars are gone. The pass also added a dark frame vignette at the left and top edges. The shells and footprint are identical, but the time of day she approved changed.

qa.name: k07m
qa.why: The three feathers, pose, curls and moon path are identical. The original already looks like a real flash photo, though. The pass warmed the cold moonlit skin to peach, added small red blemishes on her back and put dust specks in the dark sky, so it changes the light without being clearly more real.

qa.name: k09
qa.why: The face is faithful: brow scar, freckles, moles and parted lips all match, and the skin is a little less over-sharpened. The pass added a black film-gate border with rounded corners (the left edge measures 36 brightness against 66 just inside) plus dust. It also made the greens more saturated and the black sand bluish. It is usable only if cropped about 3%.

qa.name: k11
qa.why: This is the biggest realism gain in the set. The original is a low-res (1352x760), oversaturated, painted-looking HDR frame, and the pass is muted, film-like and twice the resolution. Kira's face, the mirror, the lamps and the pose all hold. But tears were added to the reflection, which turns her sensual parted-lips look into a pained one, and the red lamps are toned down. Re-run without tears and it should be USE_REAL.

qa.name: k37
qa.why: Hard reject. The pass added a person to an approved empty frame of black sand and purple foam: a crying, topless young woman with short hair who is neither Kira nor in the cast (whole-frame luma correlation 0.49). The beach and foam match underneath, but the shot is now a different shot.

qa.name: k26
qa.why: The moonlit lattice shadows are gone from both faces, her shoulder and his chest; they survive only on the right of the shirt. Exposure doubled (mean luma 45 to 94), so the night scene reads as daylight. Kira and Ule are still recognisable but smoothed and younger. Skin is less oily, but the approved lighting design is lost.

qa.name: k28m
qa.why: The approved low-key shot (face in shadow, warm rim light on the stubble) is now flat and front-lit: luma 25 to 87, saturation 0.64 to 0.30. His tanned skin went pale pink and the smoke wisps in the background are mostly gone. The hand, pose and framing are unchanged.

qa.name: k34
qa.why: The original already read as a real photograph, so the gain is small. The pass also added content: water droplets on Kira's cheek and upper arm, film-dust specks in the sky and on the sand, and a darker film-gate vignette at the edges. Faces, Ule's hand on her back, the dog and the framing are otherwise the same.

qa.name: k32m
qa.why: Structure is preserved (luma correlation 0.98) and the hand count and poses match. The original already looked like a film still. The pass mainly brightened it (luma 42 to 80) and turned the warm amber club light on the skin into pale pink, so it is not clearly better and the light colour changed.

qa.name: k25m
qa.why: Real gain: the oversaturated orange skin (saturation 0.65 to 0.35) became natural pores and drops. Changed: the amber club key light on Ule's tanned temple is now pale neutral skin, his eye at the left edge is now revealed, and the scattered white powder flecks became clear water drops (the main powder line is intact). If used, k28m and k32m should match it.

qa.name: k27
qa.why: Composition is identical (luma correlation 0.98) and the black letterbox bars baked into the original are gone. Trade-off: the warm tan skin is now cool pale neutral, and the scar reads redder and fresher. The original was already photographic, so this is a look choice for Elena.

qa.name: k36
qa.why: Kira's face, hands, feet and the foam ring are structurally identical (luma correlation 0.99 or higher). The pass adds film grain, real skin texture and freckles, with a modest exposure lift. Only side effect: a slightly bluer cast on the sand. Nothing was added or removed.
